assessment.summary: KRAS is one of the most extensively studied oncology targets, with exceptional structural coverage (556 PDB entries, best resolution 0.953Å), two FDA-approved covalent inhibitors (sotorasib and adagrasib targeting G12C), and nearly 6,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries. Druggability is high for the G12C mutant specifically, though broader mutant coverage (G12D, G12V, G13D, etc.) and wild-type KRAS remain challenging. The target is robustly validated across multiple cancer indications with an enormous and active literature base.
evidence_gaps: Approved drugs (sotorasib, adagrasib) are covalent and mutation-specific (G12C only); druggability of other common KRAS mutants (G12D, G12V, G12R, G13D) is less established clinically
Wild-type KRAS lacks approved inhibitors and has a very shallow, dynamic binding pocket, limiting pan-KRAS druggability
Median IC50 of ~1020 nM across ChEMBL entries suggests many compounds have modest potency, reflecting the historical difficulty of targeting this GTPase
Resistance mechanisms to G12C inhibitors (e.g., secondary mutations, bypass signalling via RTKs, MAPK reactivation) are emerging and not fully addressed by current agents
Allele-specific structural data for non-G12C mutants in complex with inhibitors is less comprehensive than for G12C
Clinical efficacy in KRAS G12C pancreatic cancer remains limited compared to NSCLC, indicating tumour-context-dependent druggability
No approved combination strategies that durably overcome adaptive resistance have been established
